analysis.investment_thesis: Swasth Foodtech is a tiny 2021-incorporated refined oils maker with a microscopic INR 8.88 Cr market cap and essentially zero profitability (ROE 0.17%). Refined oils is a brutal commodity business with razor-thin margins and no visible moat — there's no "story" here worth betting on.
key_strengths: High promoter holding at 72.89% signals skin in the game
FMCG/edible oil sector has persistent end-demand in India
Small base of INR 8.88 Cr could theoretically scale if execution delivers
key_risks: ROE of 0.17% is effectively zero — capital is earning nothing
Refined oils is a commodity with ruthless competition from Adani Wilmar, Ruchi, Marico
4-year-old micro-cap with no demonstrated growth story or earnings track record
red_flags: Near-zero ROE (0.17%) with no margin or growth data to justify the listing
Microcap SME on BSE — liquidity and disclosure risk
No earnings visibility makes PEG incalculable — violates my core discipline
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch GARP perspective, I need a story, a growth rate, and a PEG I can compute. Here I have none of those. A 0.17% ROE tells me the company isn't earning its cost of capital — not even close. Refined edible oils is one of the least attractive businesses in Indian FMCG: commoditized, import-parity priced, crushed by giants like Adani Wilmar and Fortune, and seasonal on palm/soy cycles. A four-year-old player at INR 8.88 Cr market cap has no pricing power and no brand moat.

I like to "invest in what I know," and what I know about refined oils is that shelf space and distribution win — not small Bengal-based manufacturers. The 72.89% promoter holding is the only positive, but alignment doesn't rescue a broken unit economic. Until this company shows consistent double-digit revenue growth with expanding margins and ROE moving toward 15%+, it's a pass. No ten-bagger lives here — just capital at risk in a hyper-competitive commodity.
